verdict: READY TO MERGE - 7 of 9 findings resolved, 2 bubbled
strengths: All relink-check tests are end-to-end behavioral: real plan.py driver subprocess against a make_project git repo, with no stubs of the vet or its helpers.
_assert_refused snapshots the plan JSON text, the ledger entry names and the base/<stem>/* tags, and requires them unchanged, so the 'writes nothing' contract is actually asserted.
Each refusal test fails against the merge base: relink --to accepted any ref before, and the old patch-id message carried 'pass --to REF' and no 'off-history'.
Problem lines are matched with the exact 'problem: at base <sha7>: ' prefix derived from the target, so the sha7 formatting is pinned too.
WALK_ROOTS = () markers are present on both script tests, and the contract test spells write-plan with SKILL.md and README.md, so the selector's anchor rule is satisfied.

vet runs after relink_target and before preflight, save, the ledger write and tagging, so a refused relink leaves the plan JSON, ledger and tags untouched exactly as the relink docstring and plan.py's module docstring claim.
vet is a required keyword-only parameter, so plan_lock stays free of config and plan_checks imports while every caller (only cmd_relink) must supply the check.
The candidate check covers both the patch-id match and an explicit --to, closing the path where --to pointed at an unrelated ancestor.
Problem lines reuse the 'at base <sha7>:' prefix of base_claim_problems, so freeze and relink refusals read the same.

SKILL.md's Relink paragraph matches the code: plan_lock.relink calls vet(new) right after relink_target and raises PlanError before preflight, the base_commit save, the ledger write and the tag (plan_lock.py:598-601). relink_claim_problems runs every time with the 'at base <sha7>:' prefix (plan.py:471-481). The doc's 'writing nothing' claim holds.

The off-history end-state wording in SKILL.md, README.md and the release note matches the reworded relink_target refusal (plan_lock.py:553-556), and it correctly limits the 'no counterpart' case to the patch-id path, so --to stays available for a known commit.
The release notes line up: the harness row reads 0.65.1 -> 0.78.1, matching plugin.json:3, and the new Changes line names the issue, the plan and both behaviors.

The plan JSON records four decisions with options and the developer's rationale, and each anchor cites file:line at the base. The receipts, the freeze ledger entry and the generated PIP page are consistent with each other (the freeze lists plan JSON blob b151dc4 and the three planned test files as ignored).
The TODO retirements are well evidenced: each close candidate gives the merging PR, the merge commit and the issue's closed state, and the counts block matches the two removed items.

The Relink paragraph matches the driver exactly: the vet runs after `relink_target` and before `preflight`, `save`, `_write` or any tag (plan_lock.py:598-601), so "before it writes anything ... writing nothing" holds for both the patch-id path and `--to`.

The parenthetical tying the relink check to the claims `check` reads at the base once an item is done, and to the base check a freeze requires before then, matches step 8 (SKILL.md:117-119) and the `relink_claim_problems` docstring.
"(or a merge commit) has no counterpart" is accurate: `patch_id_match` returns None for a commit with no patch id, and `_patch_ids` passes `--no-merges`.

The refusal text in `relink_target` repeats the skill's end-state rule and keeps `--to` for a commit known to hold the base's code, so the skill's "no `--to` is guessed" and the driver's message agree.
A contract test pins the new SKILL and README wording to the Relink-to-Archive span, so a later edit cannot silently drop the base check or the end-state rule.

plan_lock.relink takes `vet` as a required keyword-only callable and runs it right after relink_target, before preflight, save, the ledger entry and the tag, so a refusal writes nothing and plan_lock stays free of plan_checks.
relink_claim_problems reuses the `at base <sha7>:` shape of base_claim_problems, so relink and freeze refusals read alike.
The refusal tests snapshot the plan JSON text, ledger entry names and base tags and assert all three unchanged, plus the exit code and the prefixed problem line; removing the vet makes each fail.

test_plan_relink_counterpart builds a real no-counterpart history (base replaced on its parent, branch rebased onto it) and asserts both the new end-state wording and the absence of the old `pass --to REF` hint.

Docs move in lockstep: plan.py module docstring, the --to help, SKILL.md Relink paragraph, README, release notes row and line, and the 0.78.1 patch bump all state the same contract; strap_lock's hint is deliberately left per D4A.

The vet runs after relink_target and before preflight, save, the ledger write and the tags, so a refusal leaves the plan JSON, the ledger and the tags unchanged. test_plan_relink_check._assert_refused checks all three.
vet is a required keyword-only argument and plan.py is the only caller of pk.relink, so no call site misses the check (strap relink is a separate path through strap_lock).

The new tests fail without the change: without the vet, `relink --to root` exits 0, and the old message contained 'pass --to REF'. All 18 relink, archive-check and contract tests pass at head, and so do test_plan_lock.py and test_plan_archive.py.
relink_claim_problems reads the claims at the candidate whether or not an item is done, which matches what check reads after an item is done and what freeze requires before one is.

minor.summary:
Decision D4 (chosen D4A) says 'Plan relink only; file a TODO for strap relink', and its rationale says 'strap relink is tracked separately'. Nothing tracks it at the PR head: docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json has no strap-relink item (its only relink item is #313, the one this PR fixes), and no GitHub issue mentions strap relink. strap_lock.py:482 still ends its patch-id refusal with 'pass --to REF', the hint D3 names as the cause of the plan 2023 incident, and strap relink still writes a --to base without checking it. The plan JSON is frozen, so the stated tracking has to be created; it cannot be edited out of the plan.

Also (overall): Decision D4A (docs/plans/2024_Relink_Base_Validation_ActionPlan.json:271-284) chooses 'Plan relink only; file a TODO for strap relink' with the rationale 'strap relink is tracked separately', and sweep S2 (:318-323) leaves strap_lock.py's `pass --to REF` hint in place on that basis. No catalog item in docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json (which this PR edits) and no GitHub issue covers strap relink's unchecked `--to` or its hint (a search for 'strap relink' finds none), so the deferred half of issue 313 has no owner.

File the strap relink follow-up (unchecked `--to` in strap_lock relink, the `pass --to REF` hint, a candidate base lacking the spec's SKILL.md in edit mode) as a GitHub issue and add it to docs/TODO/RepoToDo.json through the add-todo flow.

minor.name: relink_claim_problems builds a record-book view nothing reads
minor.summary:
The docstring says the item statuses come from the record book's view, since a receipts plan keeps them in its receipts, and the body calls book_of(plan_file, plan).view() before the anchor and sweep checks. The check runs at the candidate unconditionally (no claims_rev branch), and plan_checks.anchor_problems / sweep_problems never read an item status (no status or DONE reference in plan_checks.py). On a receipts plan the view loads every receipt file and the DesignEvolution catalog for no effect, and the docstring sentence describes a dependency the code does not have.

Also (runtime): relink_claim_problems repeats the body of base_claim_problems: pc.anchor_problems(plan, repo, rev) + pc.sweep_problems(plan, repo, history_paths(active()), rev), each line prefixed 'at base <sha7>:'. The two now must stay in step by hand (the prefix the relink test and SKILL contract key on, the history skip list).

Also (overall): plugins/harness/scripts/plan.py:478 builds `book_of(plan_file, plan).view()` and the docstring at :475-477 says the item statuses come from the record book's view because a receipts plan keeps them in receipts. Under D1A the check runs regardless of status, and neither `pc.anchor_problems` (plan_checks.py:74, iterates every item's anchors) nor `pc.sweep_problems` (plan_checks.py:324; `moved_paths` reads only `base_commit` and only when `rev` is None) reads an item status, so the view changes nothing: on a receipts plan it loads every receipt and the DesignEvolution catalog for no effect. The docstring claim is a leftover of the D1B design (gate on `claims_rev`). The same leftover sits in tests/scripts/test_plan_relink_check.py:6-7 ('an item done in a receipt counts as done'), and the two anchor tests (:90 'once an item is done', :97 'before any item is done') present as two branches what is one code path.

Also (adv_code): When the patch-id counterpart exists but an upstream change under it shifted an anchored line, relink now refuses with an `at base <sha7>:` line. `check` fails too (the tree has the shifted line). Editing the anchor and running `freeze --refreeze` also fails, because the refreeze reads the anchors at the old base still in `base_commit`. The only route that works is not written down anywhere: hand-edit the anchors in the frozen plan, run relink (the vet reads the edited plan), then refreeze. The refusal text, the `--to` help and the SKILL.md Relink paragraph (plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/SKILL.md:186-196) describe only refusal and the squashed-base end state, so the developer looks stuck.

Attack: In a make_project repo (tests/scripts fixtures): advance_main -> old; fill + commit the freeze (anchor src/calc.py:1 'def add(a, b):'); git checkout --detach old^, prepend '# header' to src/calc.py, commit; git cherry-pick old (the counterpart, same patch id); git rebase --onto <counterpart> old feat-x. Then `plan.py relink 1` exits 1 with 'problem: at base <cp7>: anchor TASK-1 src/calc.py:1 ... line 1 reads # header'. `check 1` exits 1 with the same anchor problem in the tree. Moving the anchor to src/calc.py:2 and running `freeze 1 --refreeze` exits 1 with 'at base <old7>: anchor TASK-1 src/calc.py:2 ... line 2 reads return a + b'. Only `relink 1` run after that hand edit exits 0. Nothing in the refusal or the skill text points to that order. Probe: docs/_scratch/pr_review/0316/pr316_20261117T230910Z/probes/test_probe_relink_deadlock.py
fix: Pass the loaded plan straight to pc.anchor_problems and pc.sweep_problems, drop the book_of(...).view() line and the plan_file parameter (update the vet lambda in cmd_relink), and delete the docstring sentence about item statuses.
Keep the view only if a status-dependent rule is intended, and then make the function branch on it; otherwise the sentence must go.

Extract a helper, e.g. claims_at(repo, plan, rev) -> List[str] returning the prefixed lines, and have base_claim_problems call it after its claims_rev guard and relink_claim_problems call it directly.

Pass `plan` straight to `pc.anchor_problems`/`pc.sweep_problems` in `relink_claim_problems`, drop the `plan_file` parameter (and from the `vet` lambda in `cmd_relink`, plan.py:1055), and delete the status sentence from the docstring and from test_plan_relink_check.py:6-7.

Keep the book read but reword the docstring (plan.py:475-477) and the test module docstring to say statuses do not affect the result, and note that the two anchor tests pin the D1A 'always' rule rather than distinct branches.

In the vet's refusal (relink_claim_problems or the PlanError raised in relink), add a closing line telling the developer to correct the anchors and sweeps for the candidate base, rerun relink, then run freeze --refreeze.
State the same order (edit claims, relink, refreeze) in the SKILL.md Relink paragraph, and pin it in tests/skills/test_write_plan_relink_contract.py.

minor.name: README relink sentence breaks the paragraph's wrap width
minor.summary:
The edited line in plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/README.md is one line of about 210 characters. The lines around it wrap at about 110 to 115 characters, matching the repo's 110 line length. The text is correct; only the wrap is off.

Also (skill_package): README.md:69 joins two clauses with different subjects: "it refuses a base where the plan's anchors or sweeps fail, and a base squashed inside another pull request, which has no counterpart, stays off-history". A reader first parses "refuses ... and a base squashed ..." as one list, then hits the dangling "stays off-history". The line is also about 200 characters long, while the surrounding prose wraps near 110. `tests/skills/test_write_plan_relink_contract.py` pins only the substrings "refuses a base where the plan's anchors or sweeps fail" and "stays off-history", so a reworded version that keeps both phrases still passes.

Also (overall): plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/README.md:69 now runs to roughly 210 characters, while the surrounding paragraph wraps near 110 columns. tests/skills/test_write_plan_relink_contract.py flattens whitespace before matching, so rewrapping is safe.
fix: Rewrap the line at about 110 characters, breaking after 'Frozen or Locked;' and before 'a base squashed inside another pull request', so the paragraph's wrap stays even.

Split and rewrap README.md:68-69, e.g. "... leaves the plan Frozen or Locked. It refuses a base where the plan's anchors or sweeps fail; a base squashed inside another pull request has no counterpart, so the plan stays off-history."
Rewrap README.md:69 at about 110 columns, breaking after 'Frozen or Locked;' and after 'pull request,' as needed.

minor.name: Archive paragraph still calls every off-history line the relink cue
minor.summary: The reworked Relink paragraph (SKILL.md:186-196) makes `off-history:` the relink cue only when a counterpart exists, and the correct end state for a base squashed inside another pull request or a merge commit. The Archive paragraph a few lines later still says, without that condition, that a base off HEAD's history prints `off-history:`, "the relink cue, whether an archive reaches it or not". Archive runs after the PR merges, which is when a squash-merged base most often has no counterpart. An agent reading that sentence would offer a relink the driver can only refuse.
fix: Reword SKILL.md:219-220 to keep the condition, e.g. "a base off HEAD's history still prints `off-history:` whether an archive reaches it or not: the relink cue when a counterpart exists, the end state when none does (see Relink)".

minor.name: Module docstring claims a record-book status contract no test can observe
minor.summary:
The module docstring (lines 6-7) says 'Item statuses are read through the record book, so an item done in a receipt counts as done.' The vet that runs the claims is status-independent: plan_checks.anchors_of yields every item's anchors whatever its status, and sweep_problems reads only plan.sweeps. So the done (line 90) and not-done (line 97) tests run the same code path. A regression that bypasses the record book view and reads the plan JSON directly would still pass both, so the stated contract is unverified.

Also (tests): All three relink-check tests pin the refusal. The existing success tests in test_plan_relink_lock.py relink plans whose only anchor (src/calc.py:1) holds at any base, and they have no sweeps. A vet that wrongly refuses a good base for sweeps (for example by evaluating the wrong revision or not skipping history paths) or for an anchor on a file the base added would pass every test.
fix: Replace the sentence at lines 6-7 with 'The claims run whether or not an item is done; the tests cover a plan with a receipt-recorded item and one with none.'
Or add a case where the record book's view actually changes the outcome, if such a case exists, and assert it.

Add a test that builds the sweep plus anchor plan from _frozen_plan(anchor=True, sweep=True), rewrites the base with _plan_lock_helpers.rewrite_base (same tree, so the claims hold), runs 'relink 1', and asserts exit 0 and that base_commit moved to the counterpart.

minor.name: Counterpart refusal assertions search all of stderr and skip the 'end state' claim
minor.summary: The docstring (lines 3-5) says the refusal states that the off-history: warning is then the end state. The test checks only that 'off-history' appears anywhere in stderr and that 'pass --to REF' does not (lines 43-44). It never asserts 'end state', and it does not tie either phrase to the 'problem: no commit on HEAD's history matches base' line, so an unrelated stderr line mentioning off-history would satisfy it.
fix: Bind the problem line and assert on it: `lines = prefixed(err, "problem: no commit on HEAD's history matches base")`, `assert lines, err`, `assert "off-history: warning in check is then the end state" in lines[0], err`, keeping the 'pass --to REF' negative check.

minor.name: The `off-history:` conjunct in the skill contract test is satisfied by pre-existing text
minor.summary: test_the_relink_paragraph_names_the_off_history_end_state asserts '"end state" in relink_step and "`off-history:`" in relink_step' (line 33). The Relink paragraph already opened with 'shows as `off-history:` in `check`' before this PR, so that conjunct cannot fail. Only 'end state' pins the new text, and the test does not check that the paragraph ties the end state to the off-history warning.
fix: Assert the joined phrase instead: `assert "the `off-history:` warning is then the correct end state" in relink_step`.
